Vaping isn't too expensive, depending on the setup you want to get. Mainly it's just a higher start-up cost, but it saves you money in the long run.

It really all depends on the setup you invest in. I'd advise against the cheap $20 vape pens with the shitty tanks. That said a 1000mAH battery with a pass-through charging capability and an aspire mini-tank would work wonders. It's $30, doesn't chew through juice too quickly, the coil heads last about two to three weeks. A bottle of juice runs about $5-15, depending on the size and where you're getting it from. With the tank I suggested in this paragraph, you should get about 5-10 refills with a small bottle of fluid, or ~15 refills from a 30mL bottle.

But for a hobbyist, I'd also advise against a 'mod' with external batteries (basically what the tank screws onto is called a 'mod'), as that also requires charging ports for the batteries, buying the batteries as an additional cost, etc. I'd advise a subohm tank that fills from the top and takes coil heads with vertical coils. Vertical coils last longer and have better airflow, and don't have what's called 'spitback' where the hot juice lands on your tongue.

I have the iTazte MVP 3.0 Pro with a Tobeco Subohm Supertank - this setup retails about $80-90, and has everything I need. As a bonus, this mod doubles as an external battery pack for USB devices, because it has a USB power output on the bottom!

Down to cost comparison. A pack of 5 coil heads for the Apsire Minitank is about $10, the juice is about $10, and the battery is about $20. So overall, it's about $35-45 startup. You'll run through the juice faster than you'll run through coils. The pack of 5 coils will last about 10-15 weeks. The juice will run about $10 every two weeks. Over the course of 12 weeks, it'll be about $60 for the juice, $10 for the coils - excluding the unit - all together $70 for just running it. If you're doing a pack of smokes a day, assuming $5 a pack, that'd be $420.

It is cheaper, but has more maintenance and a higher startup cost than just smoking cigs. But the benefits in the long run are great. Plus you can dial down the nicotine doses. Start high, go lower the next week or two, then go lower the next time you refill, etc.
